players.product: gas & liquid delivery subsystems for etch/deposition tools (Lam, Applied)

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 results (non-GAAP): revenue came in at the upper end of guidance, up 15% sequentially, as volumes ramped through the quarter; gross margin rose 110 basis points sequentially on factory leverage in the integration business; operating income more than tripled vs Q4 and EPS was the highest in three years; cash from operations was a use of $2.9 million on inventory investment; cash $89.1 million and total debt $122 million at quarter end.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $256.1 million (up 15% sequentially); gross margin 12.8%; operating income $8.7 million (3.4% of revenue); EPS $0.15; EBITDA of nearly $14 million

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 guidance: management said Q2 forecast reflects unconstrained demand exceeding $300 million, one of the steepest ramps in Ichor's history (growth well over 30% in just two quarters); a quarter earlier the CEO would have guided $265 million-$270 million for Q2; demand across core markets strengthened since the last call and every quarter in 2026 is expected to be a growth quarter; OpEx run rate of approximately $25 million from Q2, with 5%-6% OpEx growth targeted for the full year.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue $290 million-$310 million (sequential growth of 17%, year-over-year increase in revenue volumes of 25% at midpoint); gross margin 13%-14%; EPS $0.25-$0.35

quarterly_data.signal: Gross margin path: management expects about 100 basis points of gross margin expansion per quarter through the second half of 2026, with gross profit dollars growing around twice the rate of revenues; ramping Malaysia (richer machining mix) and finishing footprint-realignment cost reductions are the final two steps to the near-term gross margin target; the CEO split the expansion roughly half volume leverage and half cost reductions.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 100 basis points per quarter; near-term gross margin target of at least 15%; volume leverage about 50%, cost reductions about 50%

quarterly_data.signal: Vertical integration: Ichor reaffirmed its target to exit 2026 with 35% Ichor-branded content in the systems it builds (25% exiting 2025, 15% in 2024); the next step-up is flow control, with 2026 a qualification year and first meaningful flow control revenues in 2027; Mexico and Malaysia capacity plus flow control qualifications should make Ichor capable of providing up to 75% Ichor-branded content by year-end. Global Footprint Realignment: half of planned equipment moves already installed and qualified (ahead of schedule); all substrate manufacturing steps now in one Mexico facility; valve product line achieved full customer qualification in Mexico in Q1, allowing Ichor to reinitiate valve qualifications at one of its major customers that had been on hold for capacity reasons; external supply temporarily increased while Mexico ramps.
quarterly_data.figure: Ichor-branded content 35% exit 2026 target (25% exit 2025, 15% in 2024); up to 75% capability by year-end

quarterly_data.signal: Demand drivers and visibility: technology transitions and strategic capacity expansions, largely in support of AI hyperscaling, favor etch and deposition applications and therefore Ichor; gate-all-around leading-edge logic requires a 30% increase in process steps, a significant tailwind. Ichor has hard PO coverage for about a full quarter and about 6 months of good visibility, with customers signaling growth into 2027; management expects double-digit sequential growth in the second half of 2026 and expects 2027 to be a growth year, with the supply chain as the main gate on revenue growth.
quarterly_data.figure: 30% increase in process steps for gate-all-around logic; hard PO coverage about a full quarter; about 6 months of visibility

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and supply: output is paced by supply chain first and labor headcount second, not by facilities; management said brick-and-mortar/clean room capacity could more than double last year's output and supports well above $2 billion of annual revenue, with the new Malaysia facility turned on last quarter; additional equipment is needed for Ichor-branded products (Malaysia machining build-out), making capex second-half heavy. The CEO cited some constraints and noise in the supply chain from Q1 into Q2, said the constraints Ichor is running into happen to be in the flow control space, and sees an open window for Ichor to capture share there; Ichor pre-positioned inventory in areas of risk.
quarterly_data.figure: brick-and-mortar capacity well above $2 billion; Q1 capex $7.1 million; capex managed to approximately 3% of revenue for this year

quarterly_data.signal: End-market mix: etch and deposition are growing faster than the lithography business; Ichor's lithography customer is expected to burn through inventory in Q3 (a headwind) with a pickup in Q4 (a tailwind). Non-semiconductor machining (commercial space and defense) is expected to grow faster than WFE this year, with commercial-space R&D work converting into hard POs; silicon carbide demand remains light with no major return.
quarterly_data.figure: non-semiconductor business less than 10% of revenues
